$comment: Golden cases for the SCM star. Each case asks a question in natural language and
carries the SQL that independently establishes the true answer, so the check is
'does the connector agree with the warehouse', not 'does the connector agree with
a number someone typed here last quarter'.
Reference SQL derives its own reporting month via MAX(month_key) rather than
hardcoding one — the synthetic star is as-of 30-Jun-2026 today and will roll.
Notation compliance (M = thousand, MM = million, B = billion, K forbidden) is
checked on EVERY case automatically; it needs no per-case configuration.

cases.question: What was our overall OTIF percentage in the most recent month? Give a single number.
cases.why: OTIF is the headline KPI and the one with a real arithmetic trap: the honest figure is order-weighted (SUM(orders_otif)/SUM(orders_total)), not AVG(otif_pct) across rows. A connector that averages the percentage column will land close enough to look right and still be wrong, which is exactly the failure a shape-only test cannot see.
cases.referenceSql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(orders_otif) / NULLIF(SUM(orders_total), 0), 2) AS otif_pct FROM main.supply_chain.fact_supply_chain_kpi_monthly WHERE month_key = (SELECT MAX(month_key) FROM main.supply_chain.fact_supply_chain_kpi_monthly)

cases.question: How many units were on backorder in the most recent month? Give a single total.
cases.why: A plain additive magnitude, and the case where Roman-scale notation actually bites — a six-figure unit count is where a model reaches for 'K'.
cases.referenceSql: SELECT SUM(backorder_units) AS backorder_units FROM main.supply_chain.fact_supply_chain_kpi_monthly WHERE month_key = (SELECT MAX(month_key) FROM main.supply_chain.fact_supply_chain_kpi_monthly)

cases.question: What was the average forecast accuracy in the most recent month? Give a single percentage.
cases.why: Deliberately an unweighted average, and the question says so. Pairs with the OTIF case: together they prove the connector follows the question's stated aggregation rather than defaulting to one habit for every percentage.
cases.referenceSql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(forecast_accuracy_pct), 2) AS forecast_accuracy_pct FROM main.supply_chain.fact_supply_chain_kpi_monthly WHERE month_key = (SELECT MAX(month_key) FROM main.supply_chain.fact_supply_chain_kpi_monthly)

cases.question: What was the total OTIF deduction cost in the most recent month? Give a single figure.
cases.why: Currency rather than units or percent, so the parser has to survive a symbol and grouping separators. This is also the number the cockpit's headline impact derives from, making a drift here directly visible to a user.
cases.referenceSql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(otif_deduction_cost), 2) AS otif_deduction_cost FROM main.supply_chain.fact_supply_chain_kpi_monthly WHERE month_key = (SELECT MAX(month_key) FROM main.supply_chain.fact_supply_chain_kpi_monthly)
